status.numerical_agreement_basis: Assessed on the 12 produced targets from the seed-42 runs, comparing each value with Table 1 at the precision Table 1 prints. The four parameter counts agree: 1.07, 35.5, 23.7 and 64.2 M. None of the four accuracies and none of the four losses agree: accuracy is 1.000, 0.914, 0.510 and 0.024 against 0.990, 0.990, 0.642 and 0.967. The LeNet accuracy differs by 2 of 210 test images; EfficientNetB7 is at chance level against a published 0.967. The four Penalty targets were not produced and are not assessed. The authors' subset and test split cannot be recovered, and seeds 1 to 4 show that accuracy after exactly 20 epochs varies widely between seeds, so a reviewer should weigh single-run differences accordingly.

gates.reason: The paper trains on 2,100 images, 50 per class, with a random 80/10/10 split. The supplied archive holds 14,249 images, 142 to 446 per class. Neither the paper nor the notebooks identify which 50 images per class were used, and the authors' split was unseeded, so the 210-image test set cannot be recovered.
evidence: Paper Sec. 5.1: 2,100 images, 42 classes, 50 each; random split into 1,680 / 210 / 210.
Read_data.ipynb saved output: 14,247 images loaded; train_test_split called without random_state.
Compare_nets.ipynb: 'Taking the first 50 names from os.listdir was a different subset every time the directory order changed' and 'The 2022 split was an unseeded train_test_split'.
Paper Fig. 9 and Fig. 10: the two test confusion matrices have different per-class counts, so LeNet and EfficientNet were tested on different random splits.
gates.required_action: Decide the subset rule and the split seed before any training run, and whether values obtained under them count as produced targets or as conditional evidence.
gates.resolution: Decided by a study team member before any training run. Subset: the first 50 files of each class folder in lexicographic file-name order. Split: random 80/10/10, not stratified, as in Read_data.ipynb, with seed 42 for both train_test_split calls and for weight initialization. Seeds 1, 2, 3 and 4 are run as supplementary evidence only and never replace the seed-42 values. Values obtained under these choices count as produced targets.

gates.reason: Table 1's Penalty column cannot be computed from the paper. Fig. 4 shows only a 12x12 excerpt of the 42x42 penalty matrix, and the stated formula S = -(1/N) * sum(A) yields values at or below zero, while Table 1 reports 3.017 to 3.130.

guesses_and_deviations.description: Which 2,100 of the archive's 14,249 images the paper used.
guesses_and_deviations.paper_says: Sec. 5.1: '2,100 images for 42 classes of gestures, 50 images for each class'. The selection is not described.
guesses_and_deviations.used: The first 50 files of each class folder in lexicographic file-name order.
guesses_and_deviations.basis: Compare_nets.ipynb says the original took 'the first 50 names from os.listdir'. Decided at gate ksl-subset-and-split.
guesses_and_deviations.effect: The images are consecutive frames, so the subset covers a short stretch of each class's recording. A different selection could change every accuracy and loss value.

guesses_and_deviations.description: The random 80/10/10 split and the weight initialization seed.
guesses_and_deviations.paper_says: Sec. 5.1: 'randomly split' into 1,680 / 210 / 210. Read_data.ipynb calls train_test_split twice without a seed.
guesses_and_deviations.used: Unstratified train_test_split(test_size=0.2) then train_test_split(test_size=0.5), both with random_state 42; tf.keras.utils.set_random_seed(42).
guesses_and_deviations.basis: The authors' split cannot be recovered. Seed 42 was fixed at gate ksl-subset-and-split before any run.
guesses_and_deviations.effect: The 210 test images differ from the authors'. Seeds 1 to 4 show the spread: accuracy ranges from 0.010 to 1.000 for LeNet, 0.257 to 0.962 for AlexNet, 0.110 to 0.514 for ResNet50.

guesses_and_deviations.description: Input size, color and pixel scaling.
guesses_and_deviations.paper_says: Not stated. The paper's LeNet description mentions 32x32 inputs in general terms only.
guesses_and_deviations.used: PIL convert('L'), resize((320, 120)) with Pillow 10.4.0's default resampling, float32, divided by 255; shape (120, 320, 1).
guesses_and_deviations.basis: Read_data.ipynb, the authors' original data loading. All four of Table 1's parameter counts match this input shape.
guesses_and_deviations.effect: Defines every model's input. For EfficientNetB7 see efficientnet-double-rescaling.

guesses_and_deviations.paper_says: Sec. 4 describes the classic seven-layer LeNet on 32x32 inputs; it does not give the layers used.
guesses_and_deviations.used: Conv 6@5x5 tanh, average pool 3/2, conv 16@5x5 same tanh, average pool 2/2, conv 16@5x5 same tanh, max pool 2/2, dense 120, dense 84, softmax 42.
guesses_and_deviations.basis: The LeNet builder in Compare_nets.ipynb, without its later augmentation layers. It has 1,071,162 parameters on this input, equal to Table 1's 1.07 M.
evidence: preflight-1 and full-lenet-seed42: count_params() = 1,071,162.

guesses_and_deviations.description: The AlexNet variant; neither the paper nor the notebooks give its layers.
guesses_and_deviations.paper_says: Sec. 4 describes AlexNet in general terms.
guesses_and_deviations.used: Conv 96@11x11 stride 4, BN, max pool 3/2, conv 256@5x5 same, BN, max pool 3/2, conv 384@3x3 same, BN, conv 384@1x1, BN, conv 256@1x1, BN, max pool 3/2, flatten, dense 4096, dropout 0.5, dense 4096, dropout 0.5, softmax 42.
guesses_and_deviations.basis: A widely copied Keras AlexNet. Compare_nets.ipynb says 'The 2022 version used 1x1 filters' in the last convolutional block. On this input it has 35,498,090 parameters, equal to Table 1's 35.5 M.
guesses_and_deviations.effect: Determines the AlexNet row. Another architecture with the same count cannot be excluded; the dropout rate has no parameters and is unverified.
evidence: preflight-1 and full-alexnet-seed42: count_params() = 35,498,090.

guesses_and_deviations.description: ResNet50 and EfficientNetB7 implementation, head and initialization.
guesses_and_deviations.paper_says: Named only; no head, pretraining or library is stated.
guesses_and_deviations.used: tf.keras.applications.ResNet50 and EfficientNetB7 with weights=None, input_shape (120, 320, 1), classes=42 (global average pooling and a softmax layer).
guesses_and_deviations.basis: Parameter counts 23,667,498 and 64,204,093 equal Table 1's 23.7 M and 64.2 M. Compare_nets.ipynb's log says ResNet50 'Finished from scratch with RMSprop'. ImageNet weights need three channels, and the original loading is single-channel.
guesses_and_deviations.effect: Determines both rows. If the authors used ImageNet weights for EfficientNetB7, this attempt's from-scratch training differs materially.
evidence: preflight-1: resnet50 count_params() = 23,667,498.
preflight-2: efficientnetb7 count_params() = 64,204,093.

guesses_and_deviations.description: EfficientNetB7 receives pixels divided by 255, although Keras' EfficientNet rescales by 1/255 internally.
guesses_and_deviations.used: The same divided-by-255 input as the other models, so EfficientNetB7 effectively sees values in [0, 1/255].
guesses_and_deviations.basis: Read_data.ipynb divides all data by 255 before any model. Compare_nets.ipynb, written later, warns that 'dividing first would feed it near-zero inputs', which suggests the original runs did so.
guesses_and_deviations.effect: Material. With this input EfficientNetB7 reaches 0.966 training accuracy but chance-level test accuracy. The diagnostic run with 0-255 inputs reaches 0.376 test accuracy.
evidence: full-efficientnetb7-seed42: 5/210 correct, 2 distinct predicted classes.
diagnose-efficientnetb7-raw-pixels-seed42: 79/210 correct.

guesses_and_deviations.paper_says: Sec. 5.2: 'root mean square propagation (rmsprop) optimizer'. No learning rate or other setting.
guesses_and_deviations.used: Keras optimizer='rmsprop' defaults in TensorFlow 2.8.0: learning rate 0.001, rho 0.9, epsilon 1e-7, no momentum.
guesses_and_deviations.basis: The default of the library the authors used.
guesses_and_deviations.effect: Affects all accuracy and loss values.

guesses_and_deviations.basis: Compare_nets.ipynb's log of the original runs gives 'batch 64' for LeNet and AlexNet. No value is recorded for ResNet50 or EfficientNetB7.
guesses_and_deviations.effect: EfficientNetB7 at batch 64 needed 31.8 to 34.3 GB of GPU memory. The paper's RTX 2080 has 8 GB, so the authors' EfficientNetB7 batch size, input or model must have differed from this attempt's.
evidence: preflight-1: ResourceExhaustedError on a 15 GB T4.
full-efficientnetb7-seed42: peak GPU memory 34.31 GB.

guesses_and_deviations.paper_says: Sec. 5.2: 'The training process chose 20 epochs'. No checkpoint selection or early stopping is described.
guesses_and_deviations.used: The weights after the 20th epoch, evaluated once on the test split.
guesses_and_deviations.effect: Validation accuracy of AlexNet, ResNet50 and EfficientNetB7 is still unstable at epoch 20, so the reported value depends on where training stops.

guesses_and_deviations.paper_says: Not stated. Read_data.ipynb's metadata shows Python 3.7.3 and standalone Keras ('Using TensorFlow backend').
guesses_and_deviations.used: TensorFlow 2.8.0 and Keras 2.8.0 on Python 3.10, CUDA 11.2, cuDNN 8.
guesses_and_deviations.basis: The oldest TensorFlow that this study has run on Modal's Python and GPUs; the authors' exact versions are unknown.
guesses_and_deviations.effect: Initializers, RMSprop and the Keras application models may differ in detail from the authors' versions.

guesses_and_deviations.used: NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB on Modal for every full, supplementary and diagnostic run.
guesses_and_deviations.basis: EfficientNetB7 at batch 64 does not fit in 15 GB; one GPU type was used for all models.
guesses_and_deviations.effect: None expected on the metrics beyond GPU nondeterminism.
guesses_and_deviations.status: adopted after preflight-1 failed, before the full runs

guesses_and_deviations.paper_says: Sec. 5.2: 'The batch normalization ... are applied for all the networks'. The authors' LeNet builder in Compare_nets.ipynb has no batch normalization.
guesses_and_deviations.used: The authors' builder, without batch normalization.
guesses_and_deviations.basis: The builder reproduces Table 1's parameter count. The notebook is the authors' code but was supplied privately, not released.
guesses_and_deviations.effect: Adding batch normalization would add 152 parameters, which Table 1's rounding cannot show, so the paper's actual LeNet remains uncertain.

guesses_and_deviations.paper_says: Abstract: 'more than 10122 gesture samples'. Sec. 4, 5.1 and 7: 2,100 images, 50 per class. The supplied archive holds 14,249 images.
guesses_and_deviations.used: 2,100 images, 50 per class, as the experimental sections state.
guesses_and_deviations.basis: Sec. 5.1 gives the split counts 1,680 / 210 / 210, which only fit 2,100.

guesses_and_deviations.paper_says: Table 1 and Sec. 7: 0.967. Fig. 10's confusion matrix sums to 210 with one error, 209/210 = 0.995, over 41 classes. Sec. 5.2 says it 'had no errors' and that the test matrix 'contains only 40 classes'.
guesses_and_deviations.effect: The published value this attempt compares against is itself uncertain. Fig. 9 and Fig. 10 also have different per-class counts, so LeNet and EfficientNetB7 were scored on different test splits.

guesses_and_deviations.used: Model.count_params(): trainable and non-trainable parameters, divided by 1e6.
guesses_and_deviations.basis: The name matches Keras' model summary line 'Total params'.
guesses_and_deviations.effect: None: all four values round to Table 1's.
